gloss: lazy person; someone who finds everything bothersome

definitions.gloss: lazy person; someone who finds everything bothersome; person who can't be bothered
definitions.explanation: A person who habitually avoids effort and finds tasks troublesome. Derived from the adjective {面倒|めんどう}くさい with the suffix -がり indicating a personality trait.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{面倒|めんどう}くさがりだ。
examples.english: He's a lazy person who can't be bothered with things.

examples.japanese: {面倒|めんどう}くさがりなので{料理|りょうり}はいつもコンビニ{弁当|べんとう}だ。
examples.english: Since I can't be bothered with cooking, I always eat convenience store bento.

examples.japanese: {面倒|めんどう}くさがりでも{続|つづ}けられる{簡単|かんたん}な{運動|うんどう}を{教|おし}えてください。
examples.english: Please tell me some easy exercises that even a lazy person can keep up with.

notes:
USAGE:
{面倒|めんどう}くさがり is a noun describing a personality type. It is formed from {面倒|めんどう}くさい (bothersome, annoying) + がり (a person who tends to feel a certain way). It is mildly self-deprecating and often used humorously.

GRAMMAR:
Can be used as a na-adjective modifier: {面倒|めんどう}くさがりな{人|ひと} (a person who can't be bothered).

RELATED WORDS:
- {面倒|めんどう}くさい (bothersome — the base adjective)
- {怠|なま}け{者|もの} (lazy person — stronger, more critical)
- ずぼら (sloppy, slovenly — related personality trait)
